subject.title: [Bug]: `exec` tool does not inherit `skills.entries.*.env` environment variables

question: Should explicitly configured `skills.entries.<skill>.env` keys that look like credentials be allowed into skill-owned host `exec` subprocesses without matching skill metadata?
rationale: The current code conflicts with documented host skill-env behavior for real users, but the fix changes a credential-to-executable-process boundary.

options.title: Allow explicit per-skill secrets
options.body: Treat keys explicitly configured under `skills.entries.<skill>.env` as operator-approved for that skill, while continuing to block dangerous host env names and adding regression coverage.

options.title: Require metadata declaration
options.body: Keep the current metadata-only allowlist and require skill packages to declare every credential-shaped env var they need.

options.title: Keep fail-closed and document it
options.body: Document that credential-shaped per-skill env names are intentionally blocked unless declared, leaving wrapper or broader env setup as the supported path.

recommendation.title: Allow explicit per-skill secrets
recommendation.body: Treat keys explicitly configured under `skills.entries.<skill>.env` as operator-approved for that skill, while continuing to block dangerous host env names and adding regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a security-boundary choice around the sanitizer and host exec credential behavior, where steipete has direct history.
